title: Indonesia’s free and active drift
gist: Indonesia's 'free and active' foreign policy has drifted into simultaneous deep leans toward both China (a navy stop near Taiwan, growing investment ties) and the US (a lopsided February trade deal with over 200 binding Indonesian obligations versus nine for Washington) without any strategy connecting them, leaving both powers free to spin Jakarta's actions as their own win.

insights.claim: China's defence ministry said its navy will train with an Indonesian ship in mid-August in waters east of Taiwan, prompting Taiwan's government to call the drill a 'military provocation' and Taiwan's foreign ministry to ask Jakarta to explain its participation.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: A concrete near-term flashpoint — a mid-August Indonesia-China naval drill near Taiwan — that Taiwan is treating as a political signal, worth monitoring for Taiwan-Indonesia diplomatic friction.

insights.claim: The Indonesian Navy explained only after Taiwan raised the issue that the China stop was a routine 'Passex' passing exercise by the KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai-332, which was sailing home after a separate exercise with the Russian Navy, ORRUDA 2026, held 23-28 July in Vladivostok.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: Confirms Indonesia conducted naval exercises with both Russia and, informally, China within the same voyage — evidence of Jakarta's genuinely multi-aligned posture, not just rhetoric.
insights.locator: The Indonesian Navy has since answered

insights.claim: Indonesia's explanation for the China naval stop arrived only after Taiwan had already gone public and asked hard questions, rather than being volunteered proactively, which the author argues reflects the absence of a strategic plan for managing perception.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: Reactive rather than proactive diplomatic communication is itself a risk signal — Indonesia's foreign-policy process lacks anticipatory risk management, raising unpredictability for partners.
insights.quote: The explanation only arrived once the story had already become a diplomatic problem.

insights.claim: In February, Indonesia signed the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART) with the United States, removing tariffs on almost all US goods and agreeing to buy set amounts of American farm products annually, while the US kept a 19% tariff on most Indonesian goods.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: A materially one-sided trade deal — Indonesia removes tariffs, the US keeps 19% — is now locked in, relevant to Indonesia's trade-balance and agricultural-import trajectory.

insights.claim: Legal experts who studied the ART text found Indonesia carries a firm duty more than 200 times in the agreement while the United States carries one only nine times, illustrating how one-sided the deal is.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: A quantified asymmetry — 200-plus versus nine binding obligations — is hard evidence of Indonesia's weak negotiating position with Washington.
insights.quote: Indonesia carries a firm duty more than 200 times in the text, while the United States carries one only nine times, a gap that shows how one-sided the deal is.
insights.locator: Legal experts who studied the text

insights.claim: Under President Prabowo Subianto, Jakarta has grown closer to the United States on defence while simultaneously growing closer to China on investment, infrastructure money and now naval contact, with nothing connecting the two relationships or defining how far each should go.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: Indonesia is deepening both US defence ties and Chinese investment ties simultaneously without a coordinating strategy — creates optionality but also headline and reputational risk for partners.

insights.claim: A country that walks into relations with both Washington and Beijing without its own plan does not stay neutral between them; it becomes a small piece of whichever story each side wants to tell.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: Frames the core risk of 'free and active' foreign policy without a strategy: ambiguity is not cost-free, it forfeits control of the geopolitical narrative to both great powers.
insights.quote: A country that walks into Washington and Beijing without its own plan does not stay neutral between them.

insights.claim: China can point to the Indonesian navy stop as proof a major Southeast Asian navy will work with it near Taiwan regardless of Jakarta's intent, while the US can point to the ART trade deal as proof Indonesia will accept unfair terms to stay close to Washington.
insights.speaker: Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat
insights.so_what: Both great powers can now weaponize Indonesia's own recent actions as propaganda for their preferred narrative — a reputational overhang independent of Jakarta's actual intentions.
